body:
Own-codebase translation needs checked module owners, shared array identity and complete source restoration. This PR translates JavaScript functions beside literal containers, empty Map/Set allocations and pure Number arithmetic constants, and adds standard Rust shared-array profiles including `std::rc::Rc::clone(&value)`. Whole Rust libraries retain visibility and exact original bytes for reverse translation.

A complete parser-owned CST proves each numeric constant's actual lexical name and pure initializer. Once that initializer independently checks and emits, its actual scalar static signature can bind sibling functions and recursive components. Existing arithmetic and lazy-static emitters retain rounding, NaN and signed zero. Calls, coercion, BigInt, unknown/eager owners and unsupported operators keep explicit obligations. TypeScript ownership scanning now uses the same real erasure path already used by the native binder.

Shared JavaScript decisions generate native rules and checked Links programs automatically. Both source-free codecs preserve aliases, distinct allocations, signed zero and Unicode. The original nine scalar, three associated-clone, ten refusal and six empty-allocation fixtures remain. Six numeric scope cases and six executable arithmetic predicates cover actual source restoration, ownership and Number behavior; one shared TypeScript case covers erasure and full-result parity. Native tests compare complete results/signatures and execute original JavaScript/emitted Rust only in CI.

Compiler repairs expose the existing constructor, fix private imports and independent Node observations, and retain the byte-wise sha2 0.11 formatter. Forty-four prior Clippy diagnostics have generator/decorator corrections for eight families. Complete original diagnostics and certified native sources remain Links fixtures. Current Rust tokens are source-owned after caller-entry validation, retaining all forgery refusals.

The last completed run, [39960718444](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/39960718444), finished all 97 jobs: 74 successful, three failed, two cancelled and 18 skipped. All sixteen reports and the three previously failing crate-history shards passed. The remaining independent causes were a raw-source timeout, a tooling timeout after all 173 tests passed, and an obsolete refusal for the unchanged `const LIMIT = 1 + 2` fixture. The aggregates reflect those prerequisites; native stages were skipped.

The repair starts all available complete archive workers on stored source candidates alongside fresh compiler preparation. Every candidate must equal the entire fresh generated source. All original compiler/profile/codec checks, three full CST text/binary replays and successful worker exits still precede publication or matrix allocation. Naming preflight checks every selected whole source before expensive extraction; every original per-view assertion and extractor remains. Job counts, gates, heap bounds and deadlines remain unchanged.

The arithmetic fixture retains its exact original input and round trip, expects the implemented Number-static translation, and adds independent JavaScript/generated-Rust execution of the result three. Version-sensitive checks bound active Node and Rust versions explicitly. Two incomplete operation-definition fields now recover their complete SAME original declarations from independently Git-certified modules and original registration/codec receipts. An exact inverse preserves old fragments, identities and contexts; unknown edits refuse.

Sixteen physical reports preserve all eight logical source unions and original deadlines. Package checks run alongside JavaScript tests; native jobs still depend on every JavaScript prerequisite. The catalogs contain 16,754 concepts and 8,046 source bindings, with 67 appended operations and all codec epochs through sixteen preserved. Naming retains 374 certified source epochs, 263 views and 2,113 names in five bounded Links documents. Source preservation does not establish semantic equivalence.

Draft validation before the latest commit: all 33 targeted declaration, archive scheduling, capacity, preflight and driver groups pass, plus the two changed binding controls. All twelve history authors, paired catalogs, snapshots, complete naming author/reader/serializer and eighteen ordered read-only verification commands pass. Source reconciliation preserves 60 requirement sources, 14 status reports, 831 dependency entries and all 469 requirements/490 fixture identities. The broader local binding invocation exhausted its fixed heap and one naming author timed out under observed CPU contention; both failed logs remain, targeted binding controls and an identical bounded naming retry pass. No Rust compilation, full raw workload, full naming policy or complete acceptance ran locally.

Commit `1d25066a857b16e58ed954b0cfd3a4b63c3ef902` is pushed. [CI 39971598320](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/39971598320) is queued for exact-commit native compilation/execution, parity, complete suites, full raw timing, naming policy, workloads and acceptance. Local invocation receipts are not requirement observations.

Full class/regex/initializer semantics and complete own-codebase translation remain unfinished; 77 ledger rows still lack complete implementation entry points. The [task handoff](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/1d25066a857b16e58ed954b0cfd3a4b63c3ef902/docs/handoffs/issue-199-after-pr-201-2026-10-19.md) retains the failures, repairs and receipts. Remaining scope stays in [issue #227](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/227), with grammar inference in [issue #224](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/224). No full-completion or closing claim.
title: Expand source-preserving JavaScript/Rust translation and repair CI histories
